## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical on-device PII redaction in multilingual chat, balancing speed, privacy, and simple NLP tooling.

## Key Concepts

- On-device inference
- Hybrid rule-based + ML
- Multilingual/code-switching handling
- Privacy-preserving evaluation
- Data labeling for PII

## Code Example

```python
import re
pii_patterns = {
  'email': r'[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+[.][A-Za-z]{2,}',
  'phone': r'[0-9]{3}-?[0-9]{3}-?[0-9]{4}'
}
text = 'Contact me at user@example.com'
for t, pat in pii_patterns.items():
  text = re.sub(pat, f'[{t.upper()}]', text)
print(text)
```

- Robust tokenizer handling for variable-length sequences and proper padding strategies

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical on-device NLP with multilingual support, lightweight models, privacy considerations, and a simple evaluation/rollout plan suitable for consumer apps.

## Key Concepts
- On-device inference with small footprints
- Multilingual tokenization and shared encoder
- Explainability via top features or attention proxies
- Privacy-preserving labeling and optional federated updates
- Offline evaluation and basic drift/latency monitoring

## Code Example
```javascript
// Lightweight sentiment scoring sketch (pseudo on-device)
function predict(features, weights){
  let score = 0
  for(const [k,v] of Object.entries(features)) score += (v * (weights[k]||0))
  const label = score >= 0 ? 'positive' : 'negative'
  const contributions = Object.entries(features).map(([k,v])=> ({k, v: v*(weights[k]||0)}))
  .sort((a,b)=> b.v - a.v).slice(0,3)
  return {label, explanations: contributions.map(c=>c.k)}
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the approach to handle unseen languages or domain drift?
- What metrics and evaluation strategy would you use for a tiny multilingual model in production?

## Why This Is Asked
Accounts for practical on-device NLP with multilingual support, focusing on a narrow, actionable capability rather than broad models. It tests data labeling, privacy, and lightweight deployment trade-offs.

## Key Concepts
- On-device NLP with tight storage constraints
- Rule-based expansion vs. dictionary lookup
- Multilingual (EN/ES/DE) handling
- Privacy-preserving, no-network operation
- Lightweight evaluation and rollout strategies

## Code Example
```javascript
const dict = {
  "API": "Application Programming Interface",
  "CI/CD": "Continuous Integration/Delivery",
  "SSO": "Single Sign-On",
  "UI": "User Interface",
  "SDK": "Software Development Kit"
};

function expandAcronyms(text) {
  return text.replace(/\b(API|CI\/CD|SSO|UI|SDK)\b/g, w => dict[w] || w);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure false expansions and handle ambiguous contexts?
- How would you design a minimal labeling workflow to add new acronyms post-release?
